newsitem.title: UK: Doubling of world population unlikely, study finds.
newsitem.headline: Doubling of world population unlikely, study finds.

text.p: Frightening predictions that the world's population will double to 12 billion in the next century are probably untrue, a team of international scientists said on Wednesday.

However, there will be many more old people, with the population over the age of 60 doubling, Wolfgang Lutz of the International Institute for Applied Systems Analysis in Austria and colleagues found.
"Among other things, we find that there is a probability of two-thirds that the world's population will not double in the 21st century," they wrote in a report in the science journal Nature.
They said global population would more likely grow from the current 5.8 billion to 10 billion in 2050 -- still a big increase.
The researchers, in Austria, the United States and the Netherlands, analysed fertility, mortality and migration around the world.
They found population growth rates are actually slowing down. Women, perhaps because of better access to contraception, were having fewer babies.
"Population growth will probably be most rapid in the Middle East, sub-Saharan Africa and North Africa, with a tripling of the population by 2050 and a quadrupling by 2100 likely," they wrote.

"Despite this rapid growth, there will also be significant increases in the proportion above 60 years of age. In contrast, in Eastern Europe and the European part of the former Soviet Union, population will probably decrease over the coming decades," they predicted.

"By 2050 the Pacific OECD (Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development, which groups rich and developing nations) countries and Western Europe are likely to experience little, if any, change in population size."
North America would see an ageing of its population, but not as dramatic as Europe's.

"In North America, a younger age distribution, a larger inflow of migrants, and a slightly higher fertility than in Europe is likely to result in a roughly 25 percent increase in population by 2050," they wrote.
China's population would grow by 37 percent while the Indian subcontinent would see a doubling of population and overtake China as the world's most populous region.
